description: The interaction regression model predicts crop yields by combining optimisation, machine learning and agronomic knowledge to select a small set of interactions between environment and management factors. It achieved a relative root mean square error of 8% or less for corn and soybean in Illinois, Indiana and Iowa, outperforming common machine learning methods, identified about a dozen environment by management interactions, and splits yield into contributions from weather, soil, management and their interactions. It was developed by Javad Ansarifar, Lizhi Wang and Sotirios Archontoulis of Iowa State University and published in Scientific Reports on 7 September 2021. Coverage is three US Midwest states. The article is open access under CC BY 4.0, and it states that the implementation and dataset are in the authors' GitHub repository, which was not opened; the code licence is not stated. Caveats: it was trained on three states and two crops, so transfer elsewhere needs refitting, and weekly in-season forecasts rely on weather scenarios. For simulation it provides an interpretable yield response to weather and management that can feed food supply and climate adaptation scenarios, for example estimating yield losses under drought or heat. It is related to the APSIM record in this catalogue, a process-based crop model used in the same region.
